import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price with body type
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
scatter = ax2.scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], 
                      c=df['model_year'], cmap='viridis', 
                      alpha=0.6, s=df['weight_grams']/20)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price (colored by year, sized by weight)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax2)
cbar.set_label('Model Year', fontsize=9)

# 3. Average price by brand (top 10)
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
brand_price = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)
brand_price.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=sns.color_palette("husl", 10))
ax3.set_title('Top 10 Brands by Average Price', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Brand', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. 4K video capability distribution
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
video_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax4.pie(video_counts, labels=['No 4K', 'Has 4K'], 
                                   autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 5. Weight distribution by body type
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='body_type', y='weight_grams', ax=ax5)
ax5.set_title('Weight Distribution by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_ylabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
ax5.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 6. Correlation heatmap of numerical features
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
numerical_cols = ['model_year', 'megapixels', 'max_iso', 'weight_grams', 'price_usd', 'has_video_4k']
corr_matrix = df[numerical_cols].corr()
mask = np.triu(np.ones_like(corr_matrix, dtype=bool))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, mask=mask, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', 
            center=0, square=True, linewidths=1, cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.8}, ax=ax6)
ax6.set_title('Correlation Heatmap of Numerical Features', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
